facts.statement: The type species G. latissimus was originally named as a species of Nothosaurus.
facts.quote: The type species of Germanosaurus is G. latissimus, originally named as a species of Nothosaurus.

facts.statement: Rieppel (1997) considered the species G. latissimus to be a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: Rieppel (1997) thus considered the species to be a nomen dubium in the species.

facts.statement: Germanosaurus lived in the early Middle Triassic (early Anisian stage) in what is now Upper Silesia, Poland.
facts.quote: known from the early Middle Triassic (early Anisian stage) Lower Muschelkalk of what was known as Upper Silesia, now a part of Poland.

facts.statement: The fossils date to about 247 million years ago during the early Anisian stage of the early Middle Triassic.
facts.quote: These deposits belong to the lower part of the Gogolin Formation, which is a basal part of the Lower Muschelkalk, dating to the early Anisian stage of the early Middle Triassic, about 247 million years ago.

facts.statement: Germanosaurus belongs to the family Nothosauridae.
Germanosaurus is classified as a reptile.
